title: Work-Share Desk: Kurzarbeit for American Employers
one_liner: Administer state short-time compensation for mid-size employers so they can cut hours 20-40% instead of laying off skilled staff, with workers drawing pro-rated unemployment benefits.
customer: Employers with 50-800 employees (manufacturers, distributors, engineering firms, PEO-served businesses) in states with work-share programs, buying through the CFO, HR head or PEO.
problem: Roughly 33 states have short-time compensation programs, yet take-up is tiny because employers do not know they exist and the paperwork (plan applications, weekly certifications, state-specific rules, payroll integration) is painful. Layoffs then destroy trained staff who cost one to two times salary to replace when demand returns.
solution: A layoff-versus-work-share calculator for CFOs, plus a done-for-you service. It checks eligibility, prepares the state plan, connects payroll (Gusto, ADP, Rippling) to generate weekly certification data, provides employee communication scripts and tracks the effect on the employer's unemployment account. Expand state by state and through PEOs and manufacturers' associations.
why_now: The oil shock (crude above $100, diesel near $6) and the September 2026 Fed hike, the first since 2023, are cooling consumers. Unemployment is still low at about 4.1%, so executives want to keep hard-to-replace workers and are wary of repeating the 2022-2023 layoff-then-rehire cycle.
revenue_model: $1,500-3,000 setup fee plus $10-15 per participating employee per week, or 15% of verified savings versus layoff and rehire. PEO channel revenue share.
non_obvious_insight: The program exists but nobody built the admin layer because the payoff only arrives in downturns. This is a business that sells the same product every recession and can build its state-rule database and PEO channel during the quiet years. Retention value is high precisely because the labor market is still tight.
first_30_days: Pick two manufacturing-heavy states with simple program rules (for example Ohio, Michigan or Pennsylvania). Publish a free layoff-versus-work-share calculator. Pitch 30 manufacturers via associations and PEOs and sign 5-10 at a $1,500 flat setup fee, doing the paperwork by hand at first.

title: Prize-Money Payout and Tax Withholding for Sports Tours
angle: Finance (stablecoins, payments, embedded finance, insurance gaps, household finance) x Sports, fitness, wellness, wearables, recovery
one_liner: A payout engine for pro-am tours and event organizers that KYCs athletes, collects tax forms, withholds correctly on nonresident winners, files the paperwork, and pays in local currency or stablecoin within 24 hours instead of on a 60-day wire.
customer: Organizers of tours and one-off events with international fields and $50k-$5M purses: pickleball, padel, fitness racing such as Hyrox, BJJ and grappling, trail ultras, surf and CrossFit-style competitions. Agents and athlete associations are secondary users.
problem: US-source prize money paid to nonresident athletes is generally subject to 30% withholding unless treaty status is properly documented, with W-8 forms and 1042-S filings. Small organizers mishandle this and carry penalty risk. Athletes wait weeks for wires that cost $25-45 plus FX spread. Athletes in countries like Kenya or Ethiopia often lose another 10-20% to agents, and payments to unbanked winners are a mess.
solution: A payee vault that holds W-8 and W-9 forms, treaty article claims and sanctions screening. The organizer funds the purse by ACH. The engine applies split rules for sponsor, agent, team and coach, calculates withholding by treaty and state, files 1042-S and 1099 forms, and pays out to bank accounts, mobile money or USDC wallets through partners in supported corridors. Payouts can be triggered at the podium. Each payout also creates a verified earnings record for the athlete.
why_now: Independent tours and pro-am leagues have multiplied and raised purses through 2024-26. Stablecoins are now regulated plumbing after the GENIUS Act, with the Fed proposing issuer rules on Sept 24, 2026. Circle's $400M Tazapay deal and Yellow Card's $40M raise are building local payout rails in emerging markets. The 1% US remittance tax on cash-funded transfers pushes senders toward digital rails.
revenue_model: 1.0-1.5% of purse volume, $15-25 per payee onboarding, $10 per 1042-S filed, and an FX spread. A tour paying out $10M a year yields about $150k in revenue.
non_obvious_insight: Sports' payout problem is not moving money, it is proving who is owed what and what to withhold. The rail is a commodity while the compliance file is the moat. Every payout also produces an athlete-verified earnings record, which lets a semi-pro athlete prove income for a bank, visa or insurer, something thin-margin athletes cannot do today.
first_30_days: Pick two fragmented sports with foreign fields, such as a trail-ultra series and a mid-tier pickleball or padel tour. Offer to run payouts for one event at cost. Use a fractional international-tax CPA plus Stripe Connect, Wise or Airwallex for the plumbing. Pre-build a treaty table for the top 30 athlete home countries. Charge 1.5% from the second event onward and aim for five events in 90 days.

title: Regulatory Slip Desk for Compliance Budget Decisions
one_liner: A probability-weighted deadline desk that tells compliance heads which rules will probably slip, which will not, and which controls are worth building now regardless.
customer: GCs, heads of compliance and CFOs at companies with $200M-$20B revenue facing many regimes at once (EU AI Act, CBAM, CRA, CSRD, US state privacy and AI laws). Secondary buyers are compliance-software vendors timing their sales and investors betting on delay.
problem: Deadlines have become unreliable. AI Act high-risk duties moved to 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III) and 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I) per the tracker (the Omnibus status is unverified), CSRD waves 2 and 3 slipped to 2028, while CBAM and CRA reporting did not move. Teams either overspend on rules that later slip or get blindsided by rules that hold. Law-firm alerts explain what a rule says, not whether it will arrive on time.
solution: A subscription tracker of about 100 obligations, each with the hard date, a written probability of further slip or scope cut with reasons (trilogue calendar, standards readiness, member-state transposition, litigation), and a split between 'no-regret controls' that satisfy several regimes (inventories, logging, supplier data) and 'wait for clarity' items. Trigger alerts ('if standard X is not cited by date Y, slip probability rises'). A public scored track record of every past forecast, plus a quarterly board memo.
why_now: 2025-26 was the year of delays and unwinds: the Digital Omnibus reshuffled AI Act dates, CSRD got stop-the-clock, and several US rules were dropped or vacated (background, verify). Buyers have now been burned in both directions.
revenue_model: $12-40k/year per enterprise seat pack, a $3k/year SME tier sold via newsletter, and a data feed to compliance-software vendors at $30-100k.
non_obvious_insight: Compliance is an options problem, not a deadline problem. Insiders sell obligations as fixed; the value is pricing probability and timing and finding multi-regime no-regret work. A public forecast track record is a moat law firms will not build because they cannot afford to be visibly wrong.
first_30_days: Publish a free 'Slip Index' showing the base rate of deadline moves across the 30 largest EU and US digital rules since 2023. Build a 500-person newsletter via IAPP-style and LinkedIn communities, and pre-sell 10 annual subscriptions at a $6k founder price with a money-back guarantee. Make every forecast in writing with a date.

title: Battery-Free Soil Tags Read by Drone
one_liner: Disposable soil moisture and salinity tags that need no battery and are read by drone flyover.
customer: Agronomy service providers, co-ops and specialty-crop growers with irrigated fields.
problem: Farmers face fertilizer and diesel volatility with no pricing power, yet soil data stays sparse because sensors cost too much and need batteries.
solution: Sub-$3 ambient-backscatter tags placed at planting and read from a drone or planter-mounted reader, starting with moisture and salinity and adding nitrate later.
why_now: Ambient-IoT chips scaled in 2025, and urea swinging from $400 to $850 to about $453/t makes precise input use valuable.
revenue_model: Per-tag fee plus a per-acre mapping and reading service.
non_obvious_insight: Soil sampling stays sparse because sensors are expensive. Making them disposable makes dense maps feasible.
first_30_days: Buy ambient-IoT development kits, prove drone readout at short range, and run a small field pilot on two farms.

title: Estate Planning for People's AI Agents
one_liner: Powers of attorney, dead-man switches and revocation tooling for the agents that hold standing authority over your money, email and subscriptions.
customer: Estate-planning attorneys and RIAs or family offices serving tech founders and executives who already run personal agents, followed by consumers through those channels.
problem: Personal agents now hold standing authority: card mandates, wallets, email access, autopay and negotiations. Step two: authority is tied to a living principal. Step three: death, incapacity, divorce or bankruptcy leaves agents acting on stale instructions or locks heirs out. Fiduciary access laws (for example RUFADAA) give no automatic access to digital accounts, and nobody has drafted for delegated software.
solution: An Agent Schedule for estate plans. It combines an inventory of agents, OAuth grants, wallets and mandates (via connectors), attorney-drafted clauses giving a digital fiduciary authority to pause, transfer or delete agents and limiting post-death actions, an incapacity or dead-man trigger that rotates credentials and downgrades permissions to read-only while notifying the fiduciary, and export of agent memory and logs for the executor.
why_now: Personal agents went mainstream in 2026 (OpenClaw reached about 247k GitHub stars), and agentic wallets and machine-payment rails launched in February and March 2026. The estate bar is only starting to publish AI afterlife primers, and they focus on AI personas, not delegated agents.
revenue_model: $500-$1,500 per client schedule sold through attorneys (roughly $300 wholesale), $10-$30/month monitoring, and $5k/year RIA channel licenses.
non_obvious_insight: Every technology that received delegated authority (checks, credit cards, cloud accounts) eventually got a legal instrument for the case where the principal stops existing. Agents have none yet, and the trigger events are guaranteed, so demand arrives on a calendar.
first_30_days: Draft the template with 2 estate attorneys. Pilot with 10 founders through an existing network. Build a simple inventory and revocation checklist using OAuth grant discovery for Google, Microsoft 365, GitHub and 5 agent platforms, and charge $750 per pilot.

title: Vacant-Unit Meter Watchdog and Insurance Vacancy Log
one_liner: Uses utility smart-meter data that owners already have rights to, so PMs can catch squatters, leaks and freeze risk in empty units within hours, without installing any hardware.
customer: Property managers and owners of single-family and 2-to-20-unit portfolios (100 to 2,000 doors). They already pay the utilities on vacant units and carry standard dwelling or small-building policies with a vacancy clause. Buyer is the PM's ops director or the owner. Secondary buyers later are E&S and landlord-program insurers.
problem: When a unit is occupied, the tenant is the sensor and tells you about leaks. When it is vacant you are blind for 20 to 60 days. Water damage, squatters, stolen copper, AC left running and burst pipes all happen in that window. Most property policies restrict vandalism, water damage and theft after roughly 60 days of vacancy, and the claim gets denied or cut exactly when the loss is biggest. Squatter removal is also time-critical: in many states an intruder found on day 2 is a police trespass matter, while the same person on day 30 needs a months-long court eviction. Walk-throughs are weekly at best, and the maintenance tech skips them when busy.
solution: Vacancy Vitals connects to interval electric and water data through owner-authorized utility APIs (Green Button Connect, or aggregators like UtilityAPI). The owner's account is usually the one active during vacancy, so no tenant consent is needed. Rules fire on patterns: continuous 24/7 water flow (leak), electric baseline above the empty-unit norm (someone living there, a crypto miner, a grow), a heating or cooling setpoint far outside range (pipe-freeze or mold risk), and a sudden drop to zero in a unit that should be running HVAC. Alerts go by text to the on-call tech with a one-tap 'send someone' button. The product also generates a time-stamped weekly vacancy-inspection log (data check plus a tech photo check-in) formatted for carriers' vacancy-permit or inspection conditions. That log is what preserves coverage.
why_now: Anti-squatter laws were passed in a wave in 2024 and 2025 (for example Florida and Georgia), which makes early detection more valuable. Smart-meter penetration passed roughly 70% of US electric customers. Insurers have been tightening on water-damage and vacancy exposure for several years. AI-based anomaly detection on interval data is now cheap. (Current state-by-state anti-squatter rules and utility API coverage should be verified before launch.)
revenue_model: $4 to $7 per vacant-unit-month on usage, or a flat $1 to $2 per door per month portfolio subscription. Later, insurer-paid or insurer-discounted programs: the carrier pays a fee per monitored door in exchange for lower loss ratios and a vacancy-clause waiver.
non_obvious_insight: The cheapest sensor for a vacant house is the meter the utility already installed, and the account is in the owner's name during vacancy. Nobody in proptech treats owner-account utility data as a security and insurance-compliance feed. They sell $60 leak sensors and cameras instead. The other secret is legal timing. The value is not detecting the squatter, it is detecting them in the first 48 hours, when the law treats it as trespass rather than a tenancy.
first_30_days: Recruit 3 to 5 SFR or small-multifamily PMs, offer a free 'backtest', and pull 12 months of interval data for units that were vacant. Show them the incidents the tool would have caught. These are usually a few leaks, a few unauthorized occupants and several HVAC-left-on units, each worth $1,000 to $15,000. Build a UtilityAPI-based prototype with three rules, text alerts and a weekly PDF log. Charge $99 per month per portfolio during the pilot, then convert to per-unit pricing. In parallel, talk to two independent insurance agents who write landlord programs, to learn the exact vacancy-permit language and to get a warm intro for the carrier channel.

title: Enclave Escrow: Buy Data by Measured Lift
one_liner: A confidential-compute clean room where the buyer's evaluation runs on the seller's data inside an attested enclave, and the price is set by the measured lift, so neither side reveals its asset before agreeing.
customer: Quant funds, ML teams and R&D groups buying alternative or proprietary datasets, and the small data sellers (satellite counts, AIS ship data, web panels, lab datasets) who cannot afford NDAs and legal cycles. Autonomous buyer agents are the growth channel.
problem: Arrow's information paradox: you cannot value data without seeing it, but once you see it you do not need to buy it. Sellers therefore refuse trials or overprice, buyers waste budget on blind purchases, and agents purchasing autonomously cannot sign NDAs or judge value.
solution: Seller uploads an encrypted dataset. Buyer uploads a hashed evaluation harness (a backtest, a fine-tune validation run, an accuracy test). Both run inside a CPU plus GPU trusted execution environment with remote attestation. Only a signed lift score leaves the enclave, under a per-pair query budget or differential-privacy noise to stop the score being used as an extraction oracle. A pre-agreed schedule converts lift into a license price, and payment triggers automatically if the buyer opts in.
why_now: Confidential computing on Hopper and Blackwell GPUs now runs with little performance penalty and produces GPU-signed attestation reports. Cloud providers and GPU-TEE clouds sell it off the shelf. Agents with pay-per-request data endpoints are starting to buy data blind.
revenue_model: 5-10% of transaction value, compute pass-through, $5-25k per paid evaluation for funds, and a subscription for private clean rooms.
non_obvious_insight: Sell the measurement, not the data. The thing placed in escrow is an experiment both sides commit to before seeing the result, which turns the sale into outcome-linked pricing and lets tiny sellers with no legal team participate. Bounding the lift oracle (query budgets) is the hard, defensible engineering piece.
first_30_days: Sign 3 small alt-data sellers and 2 small funds or ML teams for paid pilots. Use rented confidential VMs and a manually built harness for each evaluation. Charge $5k per evaluation and deliver a signed report. Use results to write a public 'pay for lift' pricing template.

title: Supply-Continuity Escrow for Hardware Startups
one_liner: Software-style source-code escrow, but for physical products: startups deposit CAD, BOMs and tooling data, and a pre-qualified micro-factory network is contractually obligated to keep making parts for buyers if the startup dies.
customer: Hardware startups selling to risk-averse institutional buyers (hospitals, cities, universities, fleet operators, utilities) who pay the fee, plus the buyers themselves as beneficiaries of an activation right.
problem: Procurement teams fear vendor death more than defects. A city buying 200 startup e-scooters or chargers, or a hospital buying a startup's carts or robots, has no continuity plan, so deals stall or die. When a hardware company collapses, its fleet is orphaned. The roughly 11,000 Fisker Ocean owners spent two years building their own parts supply chain through a nonprofit.
solution: A continuity package. Startups deposit CAD, drawings, BOM, supplier list, firmware build environment and key tooling data. We validate it by making trial 'trigger-ready' proof parts on printers, CNC and short-run PCB partners so that the plan is real and tested. A contract gives named buyers release rights on defined triggers (bankruptcy, 90 days with no shipments, end-of-life). Result: a one-page Continuity Letter the startup attaches to bids.
why_now: Hardware failures have piled up (Fisker, Canoo, Nikola and other consumer and mobility failures), so procurement officers have fresh horror stories. Low-cost printing, CNC and small-batch PCB fabrication now make it plausible to reproduce a wide range of parts locally without the original supply chain. Cities and health systems are buying more startup hardware in robotics, mobility and charging.
revenue_model: Annual escrow and validation fee from the vendor ($5k to $25k based on complexity), a paid proof-of-manufacturability audit, an activation fee (10% to 20% of fabricated-parts value) when triggered, and optional buyer-side monitoring of vendor health.
non_obvious_insight: It sells like insurance with a tiny loss ratio. The physical network is only activated a few percent of the time, but the deposit and the tested proof are what unlock enterprise deals for the startup. Because the startup pays to close a sale, the network is funded by growth spend rather than by rare disaster events. The hard part is proving manufacturability in advance, and that proof is the moat.
first_30_days: Talk to 10 hardware founders who are stuck in enterprise procurement and to 3 procurement or biomed managers who have been burned before. Offer a fixed-price $2,500 Continuity Letter (checklist audit plus one proof part) to the first five. Draft a simple template agreement with a startup-friendly law firm and line up two machine shops and a PCB house as network partners.

title: Earn-In Equity for Journeymen Buying Trade Shops
one_liner: A platform that turns a retiring HVAC, plumbing or electrical owner and a 25-year-old journeyman into a multi-year vesting buyout with a pre-agreed valuation formula, seller note and SBA-ready paperwork.
customer: Retiring owners of 5-40 employee trade shops (sellers pay) and licensed journeymen or foremen aged 22-35 (buyers), plus SBA lenders that fund the final tranche.
problem: Most trade-business owners plan to retire within years, yet only about half have a succession plan. Selling to private-equity roll-ups strips the local shop, and employees cannot get $1M+ loans with personal guarantees or clear the licensing hurdles. Owners hesitate to leave, and buyers lack a track record that lenders trust.
solution: An 'earn-in': the journeyman converts part of pay, bonus and sweat into equity tranches at a formula price (a multiple of trailing owner earnings with a collar), while the owner keeps a seller note and consulting role. The platform supplies valuation, legal documents, state-by-state license-qualifier planning, a data room from job and dispatch software, and a lender packet. After three to five years it supports the final SBA-financed buyout, monitoring callbacks and margins as an early-warning system.
why_now: An estimated 6 million small-business ownership transitions and up to $5T of enterprise value are expected by 2035, and Gen Z interest in trades and acquisition is rising. Lenders want buyers with operating history, which a staged earn-in builds. Field-service software now produces clean data to underwrite from.
revenue_model: A seller-paid setup fee of $4-$8k, a 1% fee on closed value plus lender referral, and a SaaS charge of $99-$299 per month for tracking tranches and KPIs. Later, a small gap-capital fund.
non_obvious_insight: The successor is already inside the business, and the bottleneck is trust and time, not capital. A formula-based earn-in makes 'when and at what price' knowable on day one, lets owners retire on a schedule, and lets buyers learn to run the shop before taking on debt. It also preserves local reputation better than a roll-up.
first_30_days: Recruit five retiring owners through local supply houses and trade associations. Charge $2,500 for a pilot 'succession blueprint' plus legal docs. Interview 20 journeymen through trade schools and union halls. Partner with an M&A attorney and one SBA lender. Aim for three signed earn-ins by month six.

title: AI-Label Pre-Flight Before You Upload
one_liner: A 'spellcheck for platform AI labels' that predicts how each service will tag and treat a file before it goes live.
customer: Social video teams, agencies, MCNs, podcast networks, and labels or distributors delivering to several DSPs, all of whom use mixed tool chains.
problem: Every major platform now labels or penalizes AI content: YouTube auto-labels (May 27), TIDAL badges and demonetizes (Jul 15), Snapchat stopped recommending fully-AI Spotlight content (Jul 31), and Spotify excludes AI persona profiles from recommendations (Aug 11). Labels can be triggered by markers in any single asset, such as one generative b-roll clip or an AI retouch, and rules differ per platform. Teams cannot predict outcomes.
solution: Upload the final export or stem set. The tool reads C2PA manifests, IPTC DigitalSourceType and XMP, runs public watermark verifiers where they exist, applies per-platform rule tables, and predicts the label and monetization outcome per service. It points to the timeline segments or assets that triggered it, drafts accurate disclosure text, and logs the result. It recommends fixes such as re-rendering a clip, and never strips manifests. Ships as plugins for Premiere, Resolve and Frame.io plus an API for DAM systems.
why_now: Platform penalties for AI labeling only became real between May and Aug 2026, and the rules differ across services. Content Credentials adoption (TikTok joined in Jul 2026) means more assets carry markers.
revenue_model: $49-499/month per team, an API at $0.02 per asset, and $2-10k/month enterprise plans.
non_obvious_insight: The market has focused on creating labels and detecting AI. Once labels carry monetization consequences, the demand is for predicting them, like SEO tools for policy. Honest teams with minor assistive AI, not cheats, are the buyers, and the product keeps disclosure accurate.
first_30_days: Build a parser on the open-source c2pa-rs library plus a rule table from published policies. Test it on 200 real videos. Offer 10 agencies a free label audit of their last 20 uploads and sell the first team plans.

title: Real Gross Margin Diligence for AI Startups
one_liner: Quality-of-earnings for agent companies: restate COGS at unsubsidized token prices, retry waste and expiring credits so investors see true unit economics.
customer: Growth-equity, PE and VC diligence teams and corporate M&A groups acquiring AI-native companies ($20M-$500M deals), and startups preparing a raise.
problem: Reported AI gross margins are flattered by free cloud and model credits, introductory rates and uncosted retries. Practitioners say diligence restates credits at renewal prices, and AI-native margins run around 50-60% versus 75-85% for classic SaaS. Agentic tasks use 5-30x more tokens, so cohort economics move fast. M&A is heating up (Okta bought Permiso for about $200M in July 2026, and Palo Alto bought Portkey and Koi). Traditional QoE firms lack telemetry fluency.
solution: Read-only connectors to billing exports, gateways, cloud invoices and product analytics. Produce cohort-level unsubsidized COGS per seat or outcome, sensitivity to price cuts and model swaps, tokens per customer growth, cost of failed runs and retries, and scaling curves. Five-day turnaround report, plus quarterly monitoring for fund portfolios.
why_now: An AI M&A wave and investors pricing trajectory over current margin. Credit-inflated margins matter more as promotional pricing expires, and 73% of enterprises overran AI budgets.
revenue_model: $15-$40k per diligence engagement and $3-$8k/month portfolio monitoring subscriptions for funds.
non_obvious_insight: The margin story is hidden in gateway and billing logs, not the general ledger. Buyers pay a premium to avoid overpaying for subsidized revenue, and every engagement builds a private benchmark of credit-adjusted margins.
first_30_days: Write the data-request list and report template. Pitch 20 growth-stage funds and deal associates, deliver 2 discounted diligence reports, and publish an anonymized credit-adjusted gross margin benchmark to generate inbound.

title: Burn Boss: Prescribed Fire as a Service
one_liner: AI burn-window planning, permits, drone ignition crews and liability cover, so landowners can safely burn and insurers can pay for the risk reduction.
customer: Private landowners, ranchers, timber owners, prescribed burn associations, water districts and utilities in TX, OK, OR, CA and CO. Insurers and reinsurers later pay for outcomes.
problem: Prescribed fire is the most effective fuel-reduction tool and the least scaled. Barriers are burn-plan expertise, weather windows, permits and smoke filings, liability insurance and crew logistics, not the fire itself.
solution: Start with a burn-plan generator and weather-window alerts built on AI forecast ensembles, plus a permit and smoke-filing packet, sold to burn associations. Then add a drone-ignition operator network and a liability wrap through a partner MGA. Add verified before/after fuel maps that insurers can underwrite (check state burn-liability rules).
why_now: AI weather models became operational in 2025 (such as ECMWF's AIFS), drone aerial ignition has matured, and record reinsurance capital wants provable mitigation. Several states have been reforming burn liability law (verify).
revenue_model: $1-3K per burn plan, per-acre service fees, and later outcome payments from carriers or utilities.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is planning and liability, not fire. Insurers can pay because treated acreage lowers their probable maximum loss.
first_30_days: Join 3 burn associations, ship window alerts and the plan generator, and run 5 paid burns.

title: Gate-Risk Radar for Evergreen Private Credit
one_liner: A quarterly shadow NAV and gate-probability score for every non-traded BDC and interval fund, sold to the RIAs and OCIOs who put clients into them.
customer: Independent RIAs and family offices ($100M to $3B AUM) with client money in non-traded BDCs, interval and tender-offer funds, at $400 to $1,500 per month per firm. Secondary buyers are TAMPs and wealth platforms (API license) and 401(k) advisers as alternatives enter defined-contribution plans.
problem: Advisers learn a fund has gated from a sponsor letter after the tender window closes. In Q1 2026 non-traded BDC investors requested about $13.9B and got about $7.4B. Blackstone gated BCRED in June 2026 with about 5% fills, and Q2 requests hit a record 12.4% of NAV with only 38% filled. Reported NAVs are smoothed, and nobody tells an adviser whether the next tender will be pro-rated or what to file.
solution: Ingest the tender-offer filings (window and cap), 10-Q and N-PORT marks, non-accruals and PIK share, listed-BDC discount to NAV, secondary bids on non-traded shares, and loan-index prices. Output three things per fund: (1) shadow NAV against reported NAV, (2) probability that the next tender gates and the expected fill rate, (3) a 'if I request X, expect to receive Y' calculator. Add compliance-ready client letters. Start as a public tracker of about 40 funds, then put the alerts and calculator behind a paywall.
why_now: 2026 is the first year pro-rata gating hit the whole non-traded BDC category. Blue Owl merged a non-traded BDC into its listed sibling under redemption pressure. The August 2025 executive order opening 401(k)s to alternatives is about to push far more retail money into these wrappers. Private-credit blowups in late 2025 turned advisers from curious to scared.
revenue_model: Tiered subscription for advisers, an enterprise API for wealth platforms and TAMPs, and a $250 per-fund 'client-ready due diligence memo' for compliance files.
non_obvious_insight: Pro-rata gating makes over-requesting the dominant strategy. Once investors expect a 14 to 38 cent fill, they file bigger requests than they need, so request size becomes a self-amplifying signal. It overstates true demand but predicts fill rates well. The gap between the listed-BDC discount and reported NAV leads request size by about a quarter. Quants see this as a bank-run game with strategic complements, not a credit-loss story, and nobody in wealth tech models it that way.
first_30_days: Scrape EDGAR tender-offer, 10-Q and N-PORT filings for about 40 funds and publish a free weekly 'gate watch' on LinkedIn and Substack framed as research. DM 100 RIA compliance heads and CIOs. Convert 10 to a $500-per-month pilot and start talks with two wealth-platform data teams.

title: Weaver Ant Crews for Cashew and Mango Orchards
one_liner: Orchard pest control by living ant colonies: trained local 'ant agents' seed, feed and maintain weaver ants in smallholder cashew and mango trees, and the farmers get paid a residue-free premium.
customer: Smallholder cashew and mango cooperatives in Vietnam, Tanzania and West Africa, and the processors and exporters who need residue-free nuts and fruit.
problem: Smallholders spray expensive pesticides to fight coconut bugs, mirids and thrips. Costs are high, farmer health suffers, and exporters worry about residue limits. Biological control from imported predators is out of reach for smallholders.
solution: Weaver ants (Oecophylla smaragdina and O. longinoda) are territorial predators that guard trees against most pests. Our agents seed colonies, connect tree crowns with rope bridges, and supply sugar and protein supplements in the dry season. Cooperatives sign a per-tree, per-season contract. A phone-based check of nest counts and canopy occupancy generates a verified 'pesticide-free days' record that supports premium pricing with buyers.
why_now: Field research already supports it. In Vietnamese mixed pomelo and orange plantations, lower costs from ant treatments produced profit gains of 47% over pesticide plots. Economic studies of African weaver ants exist for Tanzanian cashew, and Vietnamese cashew smallholders (more than 200,000 households) are pesticide-dependent. What is new is cheap phone-based computer vision to verify colony presence, and buyers tightening residue limits.
revenue_model: A per-tree, per-season service fee set below current spray spend, plus a share (for example 10-15%) of any quality or premium uplift negotiated with exporters. Buyers can also pay a per-tonne residue-free supply fee. Ant-agent franchises would scale the model through local micro-entrepreneurs.
non_obvious_insight: Weaver ants were the world's first documented biocontrol, used in Chinese citrus groves for about 1,700 years. They never scaled because no one can patent or sell a colony, so there was no way to capture the value. The business is not the ant; it is the service wrapper, the verification data and the offtake contract that let someone get paid for a free natural crew.
first_30_days: Sign one cooperative in a cashew belt (Binh Phuoc in Vietnam or Mtwara in Tanzania). Recruit and train 20 farmers and 3 ant agents. Seed 500 trees in a pilot and compare pesticide spend and nut quality on matched control rows. Ask one processor to pre-commit to a residue-free premium.

title: Babel Tables for Multilingual Community Programs
one_liner: A tabletop translation hub that lets a senior-center lunch, ESL class or church group hold one conversation across four languages in real time.
customer: Senior centers, Area Agencies on Aging, libraries, faith groups and community colleges in multilingual cities, paying $150-300 a month per site plus hardware, funded from language-access and aging-services budgets.
problem: More than 25 million Americans have limited English proficiency, and isolated immigrant elders sit in language-siloed programs or nowhere. Interpreters cost $60-120 an hour, so programming stays segregated by language, blocking intergenerational and cross-cultural ties. Asian adults were the only Pew group net positive on chatbots for loneliness (37% help, 25% hurt), which signals openness to tech-mediated connection.
solution: A 4-microphone puck plus tablet that separates speakers and streams speech-to-speech translation to earbuds or phones, and captions on a table screen, for up to four languages at once. 'Table mode' runs low-stakes conversation card games, 'host mode' supports classes. Audio is processed ephemerally, with a human interpreter fallback for high-stakes moments.
why_now: Speech-to-speech translation reached conversational latency and usable quality in 2025 (translation in earbuds and meeting platforms), and small on-device models make private processing possible. State and city language-access mandates persist. Loneliness is a WHO-measured metric.
revenue_model: Hardware plus per-site SaaS, per-language add-ons, and contracts with city aging departments and Area Agencies on Aging.
non_obvious_insight: Translation tech was sold as an accommodation for one person and one interpreter. The bigger use is mixing: making the group itself multilingual so a Cantonese widow, a Spanish-speaking teen volunteer and an English-speaking regular can share one table. The unit of value is the table, not the user.
first_30_days: Prototype with a $200 speakerphone and a phone app. Pilot 'Table Tuesdays' in two senior centers (Chinese, Spanish, English) through a city aging department. Collect participation data over four weeks and charge $99 a month.

title: Contingency Water-Bill Recovery for Small Commercial Sites
angle: Pairing 1: SMB back office x Water (lens: bookkeeping x utility tariffs)
one_liner: A no-win-no-fee service that rebuilds small commercial sites' water, sewer and stormwater bills from the local tariff and claws back irrigation-sewer overcharges, leak credits and stormwater-fee errors.
customer: Owner-operators of small multi-tenant commercial properties (strip centers, 20-200 unit apartment communities, self-storage), churches, private schools and nurseries in cities that bill sewer on metered water and charge stormwater fees. Start in one drought metro. Referral partners are their bookkeepers and property managers.
problem: A $5k-$40k/yr water bill is too small for utility-audit firms, who chase national chains, and too tangled for the bookkeeper, who codes it and pays it. Tariffs sit in council resolutions. Scarcity tiers and surcharges keep changing. Sewer is often billed on metered water that includes landscape water that never reaches the sewer. Stormwater fees rest on impervious-area estimates that are often wrong. Leak-adjustment windows lapse unnoticed. The Fed's 2026 small-business survey names rising costs the #1 financial challenge.
solution: The owner forwards bills or connects QuickBooks/Xero and the utility portal. An LLM pipeline reads the tariff PDF and rebuilds every bill. It flags misclassified meters, irrigation on sewered meters, overnight-flow leak periods in interval data, impervious-area disputes (checked against aerial imagery) and estimated reads. A human analyst files the credit, refund or reclassification with the utility, chases it to cash, and writes corrected coding back into the books. Wedge product: an 'irrigation-sewer plus stormwater credit audit' for one metro and three utilities.
why_now: 49.6% of the US was in drought on Sept 24, 2026 after the warmest June-August on record, so scarcity pricing and surcharges are multiplying. Regulated private water companies invested about $6.8B in 2025 ($43.5B over the decade) and recover it through rate cases that small customers never see. LLMs make it cheap to read hundreds of heterogeneous tariffs and bills. Customer portals increasingly expose interval meter data. Intuit and Xero are rebuilding around LLM subscriptions and cannot easily take contingency fees.
revenue_model: 30% of verified first-year savings plus recovered refunds (contingency). Then a $25/site/month monitoring plan that stops corrections regressing and catches new leak periods. White-label for property managers at about $8/door/year.
non_obvious_insight: The one-time refund is the hook, not the product. The value is the permanent reclassification of the account (meter class, irrigation split, impervious area), which lowers every future bill. The moat is a tariff library that human auditors cannot afford to build for accounts this small. Outcome-priced work does not fit subscription incumbents, so the real competitor is nobody.
first_30_days: Pick one metro with a published stormwater-credit manual and an irrigation or deduct-meter option. Hand-collect five utilities' tariffs. Recruit 20 owners through the local apartment association or BOMA chapter and 5 bookkeepers who get a 10% referral. Audit 24 months of bills per site with the LLM pipeline plus one analyst, with no upfront fee. Targets: 10 audits by day 30, first 3 recovered checks by day 60, then publish anonymized results as the sales asset.

title: Signed Authority Certificates for Buying Agents
one_liner: Companies issue legally strong, machine-verifiable certificates saying which agent may order what, up to what amount, from whom, so suppliers can trust agent-placed orders.
customer: EU industrial distributors and wholesalers that receive purchase orders by email or EDI, and their larger business customers deploying procurement agents. Start with DACH and Benelux distributors.
problem: A supplier gets an order from 'Acme's purchasing agent' and has no way to know it may bind Acme to a EUR 50k purchase. AI makes fake purchase orders and business email compromise cheaper. Consumer-oriented agent-payment mandates (AP2, TAP, Verifiable Intent) do not cover B2B signing authority, and research notes from 2026 say agents do not map cleanly onto EU digital wallet categories.
solution: An authority registry and issuance service. A company's legal representative signs a delegation certificate (qualified electronic signature via eIDAS trust providers, EUDI wallet later) covering agent key, scope (categories or SKUs), per-order and monthly limits, validity and revocation. Suppliers verify by API in under 200 ms and see remaining limit. Integrate with ERP order intake and e-invoicing. The signed record is court-grade evidence in disputes.
why_now: EU member states must offer digital identity wallets by end-2026, financial institutions are expected to accept them by December 2027, and qualified signatures already carry the legal effect of handwritten ones. Agent mandate standards exist but are consumer-centric.
revenue_model: EUR 99-499/month per issuing company, EUR 0.05-0.20 per supplier verification, and enterprise licenses.
non_obvious_insight: Legal effect, not cryptography, is the scarce ingredient in B2B agent commerce. The EU uniquely has an instrument (the qualified signature) that turns a delegation into evidence courts accept, so build where the law already does the hard part.
first_30_days: Integrate with one qualified trust service provider for signing. Interview 20 distributors about agent-placed orders and PO fraud, pilot with 3 distributors and their top buyers on existing order intake, and collect letters of intent.

title: Workout GC for Stalled Spec Homes
one_liner: A finish-the-house crew and re-sequencing service sold to construction lenders, not builders, for homes stuck at 40-90% complete.
customer: Community banks, credit unions and private construction lenders with spec-home loans being extended (Texas, Florida, Southeast, Mountain West). Secondary customer: distressed small builders referred by those lenders.
problem: Starts hold at 1.275M SAAR but completions fell 27.1% YoY. One executive described 15-20 houses stuck on foundations for 6+ weeks, and a West Virginia builder risks about 40 closings. The builder cannot get crews back, and the lender holds the real risk: exhausted interest reserves, mechanic's liens, extensions, and half-built collateral. Lenders have no operating arm.
solution: Start with a flat-fee stuck-loan triage: site visit, photo scan, cost-to-finish, days of carry and sub availability, ranked across the lender's watchlist. Then take over scheduling and finishing on cost-plus. A few in-house supers plus a pre-vetted bench of framing, MEP and finish subs are paid in 7 days through the lender's normal draw process. The builder keeps the lot and the sale. A bonus is paid per day saved before the extension deadline.
why_now: Completions are down 27.1% while starts hold. 63% of builders already use incentives and 35% cut prices, so there is no margin left to absorb delay. ICE arrests rose from 32,545 in May to 49,571 in July 2026 and are pulling crews off sites. 2027 starts are forecast down 2-4%, so more small builders will stall. The 2024-25 vintage of spec construction loans is maturing now.
revenue_model: $2.5K per-loan triage or $15K portfolio review. Finishing work at cost plus 12-15%. Success fee of about 1% of loan balance for closing before the extension deadline.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone frames stalled homes as a builder or labor problem. The party with the budget, the legal leverage and no ego is the lender, who cares about loan resolution rather than building. Subs return when someone credible promises six straight days of work and pays in a week. A lender-backed GC has that payment credibility and the stalled builder does not.
first_30_days: Call 15 construction lenders and workout officers through state bankers associations. Offer two banks a free 10-loan triage. Hire two ex-superintendents. Line up 3 framing, MEP and finish subs per metro on a 7-day-pay promise. Target a first paid contract on 1-3 homes by day 30.

title: Resolution-Risk Ratings for Prediction Market Contracts
one_liner: A credit-rating-style score for how likely an event contract is to resolve ambiguously or be disputed, plus the rulebook basis between 'identical' contracts on different venues.
customer: Prop desks, market makers and arbitrage funds trading Kalshi, Polymarket and newer venues, at $300 to $3,000 per month. Venues and market creators pay for pre-listing rule linting.
problem: Polymarket logged more than 1,150 disputed markets in the first half of 2026, more than all of 2025. A US-Iran peace-deal market with over $345M in volume split traders on whether the outcome met a 'permanent' deal. Cross-venue arbitrage is not risk-free because sources, cutoffs and definitions differ, and displayed depth can vanish. Everyone prices the event, but nobody prices the contract wording.
solution: Parse each contract's rules (source of truth, timestamp cutoff, key definitions) and compare against a labeled history of disputes and oracle overrides. Output a 0-100 Resolution Risk Score with an expected haircut in cents. Give matched cross-venue pairs a scenario table of where they would settle differently, so arbitrageurs size positions correctly. Offer a 'rule linter' that flags ambiguous phrases for market creators, and deliver everything through an API and Discord/Telegram alerts.
why_now: Prediction-market volume is exploding (Kalshi reportedly passed $100B) and dispute counts are rising sharply. Institutional market makers are arriving and need risk inputs beyond price. Regulators and states are still fighting over these contracts, so rulebook and venue risk is priced by no one.
revenue_model: Desk subscriptions, per-market audit or lint fees from venues and market creators, and a data license to aggregators and terminals.
non_obvious_insight: Credit derivatives already lived through this. The asset's definition, meaning restructuring clauses and Determinations Committee rulings, became a priced factor, and an entire professional infrastructure grew around it. Prediction markets are at the 2003 CDS stage: the basis between 'identical' instruments is definitional risk. The winner is the rating-agency-plus-dispute-committee layer, not another odds aggregator.
first_30_days: Scrape resolved and disputed markets and hand-label about 300 disputes into an ambiguity taxonomy. Publish a public weekly 'Dispute Watch' with two or three calls that prove right. Sell to five arbitrage-bot shops through their Discord and Telegram communities at $500 per month. Offer free linting to prolific market creators for testimonials.

title: Live Lyric Captions for Concerts
one_liner: Setlist-conditioned real-time captions of sung lyrics and banter, delivered to phones and smart glasses with translation, sold to venues as an accessibility service.
customer: Venues, festivals and touring promoters with accessibility obligations, plus artists wanting international fans served.
problem: Deaf and hard-of-hearing fans get no lyrics, because speech recognition fails on singing over a loud PA. Human captioning exists for spoken theatre but not concerts, and overseas fans lack translation.
solution: Load the artist's setlist and lyrics ahead of time. Align the sound-desk audio to lyrics with tolerance for improvisation and run speech recognition only on banter. Distribute via a QR-code web page and smart glasses with per-language translation, with a human captioner supervising deviations.
why_now: Display-equipped smart glasses started shipping in late 2025, on-device translation is good enough, and venues face growing accessibility pressure.
revenue_model: $300-1,500 per show for venues plus a paid translation tier from artists' fan clubs, and sponsorship from device makers.
non_obvious_insight: Lyrics are the one thing known in advance, which turns an impossible speech recognition problem into a tractable alignment problem. Accessibility budgets exist but nobody sells a concert-native product.
first_30_days: Test at 3 local shows with two Deaf community groups. Partner with one venue for a free pilot, gather testimonials, and sign 2 venues at $250 per month.
